analysis: Aminoglycosides are a class of antibiotics known for their ototoxic effects, which primarily target the cochlear hair cells. The consensus in medical literature is that aminoglycosides predominantly affect the outer hair cells in the basal area of the cochlea. This area is more sensitive to the effects of these drugs, leading to high-frequency hearing loss. The basal region of the cochlea is responsible for detecting high-frequency sounds, and damage here is consistent with the clinical presentation of aminoglycoside-induced ototoxicity. Inner hair cells and the apical area are less commonly affected by aminoglycosides. Therefore, the most likely correct option, based on standard medical knowledge and consensus, is that aminoglycosides affect the outer hair cells in the basal area.
